summary: Harold Walter Bailey (1899–1996) was an Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Western Australia and the University of Oxford under Frederick William Thomas, later holding posts at SOAS and the University of Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani (1891–1980) was an Indology and history scholar. Educated at Aligarh Muslim University and the University of Oxford, and mentored by Ghulam Yazdani, he served at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).
Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied under Chandrabhāl Tripathi and held posts at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe (1932–2020) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and served on the faculty at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist. He served as head of the Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (attested 1989) and worked in the Oriental Department of the Prussian State Library (attested 1992–1994).

Haruhiko Masaki (b. 1938) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo, and he later served as a professor at Nagasaki University (~1978–2003).
Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1980–1990) and the University of Tokyo (~1990–2007).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her MA and PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson (b. 1965) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Groningen and Leiden. He has held positions at Groningen, Oxford, the University of Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and the University of Hamburg (teaching 2000–2002; professor from 2006).

Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and served as professor and dean at Musashi University (1968).

Harvey B. Aronson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and co-director at Dawn Mountain Center (attested 2001).

Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and attended Otani University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. He served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954) and Shinshu Otani-ha (1951–1952).

Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London and was supervised by Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, also studying under D. C. Lau and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Heeraman Tiwari (b. 1961), an Indology and philosophy scholar, studied at Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He has held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1996), Heidelberg (2011–2012), and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2014–2015).
Hegoda Khemananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal of Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director of Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld (b. 1970) is a Tibetology scholar. She earned her doctorate under the supervision of Signe Howell at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006), where she subsequently held a postdoctoral fellowship (~2007–2010).

Heidi I. Köppl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi Pauwels (b. 1963) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Washington under Alan W. Entwistle, lectured at SOAS (1994–1996), and became a professor at the University of Washington (1996–2009).

Heike Oberlin (b. 1970) is an Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Kerala Kalamandalam, and Würzburg. She held positions at Tübingen (2005–2008), served as Scholar in Residence at Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and was a guest professor at Sapienza University of Rome (2025).

Heiner Eichner (1942–2024) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1967–1974) and later held a post at the University of Vienna (~1989–2010).
